- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after spikes.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, reduce forecast mean by 2–5% to account for policy-induced downward pressure.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model should slow trend decay to avoid overcorrection; add 1–2 days lagged momentum to forecast.
- When event count is high and supply net is negative, forecast should be anchored to 1–2 prior low points unless sentiment is strong bullish.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should avoid smooth linear trends and allow for volatility clustering in forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent volatility pattern, not just mean.
